title: [Auto Hide Cursor] Pointer stays hidden while an elevated (admin) window is in the foreground
summary: Auto Hide Cursor reportedly remains globally hidden when a medium-integrity worker misses mouse input over an elevated foreground window. The existing timer receives cursor coordinates but never restores a hidden cursor.
next_action: Consider for the coordinator's bounded design batch; first reproduce using physical pointer movement and verify timer recovery requirements.

judgment.rationale: The reporter provides two concrete elevation-sensitive reproductions and a controlled normal/elevated comparison. Current state code has no timer-based recovery once hidden. A bounded movement-recovery design is justified, but the integrity-level mechanism and real pointer behavior still need maintainer verification; no full design or implementation has been completed.
evidence: The report supplies typing and idle reproductions on 0.102.2862.0 Insider, a normal-window control, measured hook/position differences, and confirmed workarounds of elevated PowerToys or disabling Auto Hide Cursor.
State.OnTimer returns None when m_hidden is true; State.OnMouseInput is the normal input restoration path.
The worker polls cursor position on its existing 100 ms timer, providing an independent observation point.
Merged PR 50803 removes injected-event filtering for touchpad recovery; it does not add restoration when the hook receives no movement callbacks.
judgment.recommended_action: Consider for the coordinator's bounded design batch; first reproduce using physical pointer movement and verify timer recovery requirements.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked issue fix, matching upstream PR, or existing fork issue/PR/branch covers missed-hook recovery. PR 50803 addresses delivered injected callbacks, not absent callbacks.

proposed_fixes.title: Recover a hidden cursor from independently observed pointer movement
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Confirmed code gap: OnTimer ignores all positions once hidden, leaving normal recovery dependent on OnMouseInput. The reporter's elevated-window callback loss is a supported but not independently reproduced explanation for reaching that gap.
plan: First reproduce the report on 0.102.2862.0 with a non-elevated runner, physical mouse movement, and normal/elevated foreground controls; compare hook delivery against successful position polling.

In AutoHideCursorWorker.cpp, make cursor-position acquisition report failure rather than representing a failed GetCursorPos as coordinate (0,0); preserve the existing single-threaded state/action queue.

In AutoHideCursorState.h, evaluate valid sampled movement while hidden before the OnTimer early return; reuse the intentional-movement threshold, request Show, and reset idle timing so the next tick cannot immediately re-hide. Cover typing-only mode as well as idle mode.

Add AutoHideCursorStateTests.cpp cases for hide-on-typing then timer-only recovery, idle hide then timer-only recovery, unchanged/sub-threshold positions, post-recovery idle delay, and absence of false movement from failed samples.
Verify compatibility with PR 50803: delivered synthetic/touchpad movement must continue restoring the cursor. Do not require administrator execution as the default repair.
verification: Build and run the native Auto Hide Cursor state tests using the repository build/vstest workflow.
For both triggers, compare non-elevated and elevated foreground windows with a non-elevated PowerToys runner; move a physical pointer after hide and confirm visibility returns without changing focus.
Repeat with typing-only and idle-only configurations, stationary/sub-threshold jitter, multi-monitor coordinates, and touchpad input; confirm restoration and no immediate re-hide.
Verify disabling/stopping the utility and existing worker failure/restore paths still restore the system cursor scheme.

confidence.rationale: The missing recovery branch is directly visible and the report includes a strong control comparison. Runtime integrity-boundary behavior, physical versus injected input and sampling edge cases remain unverified; this is a fast-pass candidate, not a converged design.

issue_context.summary: Auto Hide Cursor reportedly remains globally hidden when a medium-integrity worker misses mouse input over an elevated foreground window. The existing timer receives cursor coordinates but never restores a hidden cursor.
known_information: The report gives precise typing and idle steps, Windows 11 build 26300.9711 and non-administrator PowerToys 0.102.2862.0.
The reporter says the pointer restores over a normal foreground app but remains hidden over an elevated app, and elevation of PowerToys or disabling the utility works around it.
The reported measurements use injected moves from an elevated helper; they are reporter evidence, not maintainer-run proof of physical-input behavior.
Current OnTimer receives a position but returns without restoring whenever hidden; the worker invokes it on its existing 100 ms loop.
No assignee, linked fix or matching fork trace was found; Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage and Product-Mouse Utilities are present.
inferences: Missing hook callbacks across the integrity boundary plausibly strand the hidden state, but the exact OS/hook cause is not independently confirmed.
A guarded position-sampling recovery path is likely to mitigate this failure without demanding administrator execution; input semantics and idle timing must be verified.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter provides two concrete elevation-sensitive reproductions and a controlled normal/elevated comparison. Current state code has no timer-based recovery once hidden. A bounded movement-recovery design is justified, but the integrity-level mechanism and real pointer behavior still need maintainer verification; no full design or implementation has been completed.
initial_investigation: Pinned State.OnMouseInput restores after intentional movement, whereas OnTimer ignores an already-hidden state: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/1b33221dfa19f30d71409eb550807883fb27283a/src/modules/MouseUtils/AutoHideCursor/AutoHideCursorState.h#L95-L123

Worker.Run already samples positions for OnTimer, and its helper does not check GetCursorPos success: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/1b33221dfa19f30d71409eb550807883fb27283a/src/modules/MouseUtils/AutoHideCursor/AutoHideCursorWorker.cpp#L129-L166
Current MouseHookProc accepts injected movement; merged https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/50803 fixes an earlier delivered-input filtering problem, not missing callback delivery.
Upstream issue timeline, issue-number PR searches, topical cursor/elevation searches, fork issue/PR searches and fork branch inventory found no existing implementation for this report.

reproduce.title: Compare Auto Hide Cursor recovery over normal and elevated windows
reproduce.version_requirement: Start with reported 0.102.2862.0 Insider; repeat against current source when preparing a fix.
prerequisites: PowerToys running as the interactive user without administrator elevation.
Permission to open an elevated Windows Terminal; a physical mouse or touchpad.
setup: Save work and keep a non-elevated window available to recover pointer visibility.
Enable Auto Hide Cursor with hide-on-typing; test hide-on-idle separately.
Use physical movement first; keep injected-helper measurements as a separate control.
steps: 1. With a normal foreground app, type to hide the pointer, then physically move it; record recovery.
2. Press Win+X then A to open Terminal (Admin); after the keypress hides the pointer, move physically over the elevated window and record whether it returns.
3. If UAC changes the sequence, use the independent idle variant: put elevated Terminal in front, wait for the configured idle timeout, then move physically.
4. Return focus to a normal app and record recovery; disable Auto Hide Cursor if needed to restore visibility.
5. In a maintainer debug session, compare MouseHookProc delivery and valid GetCursorPos samples while hidden in both controls; do not replace this with a compile-only check.
6. Repeat after an eventual candidate change and confirm recovery works for both triggers without immediate re-hide; retain touchpad/injected-input coverage from PR 50803.
reproduce.expected_result: Physical pointer movement restores the global cursor over either integrity-level foreground window without a focus change; the normal-window control remains unchanged.
